planting.note: Set rhizomes in loose, mineral-rich mud or fine gravel at the shaded margin of a warm-climate pond or bog filter with the crown at or just below the waterline; elsewhere grow submersed in an aquarium or as an emersed paludarium plant and overwinter indoors.

directions: Native to slow, shaded streams and flooded rice paddies of Sri Lanka, this rhizomatous aroid grows equally well fully submersed in an aquarium, fully emersed as a shaded bog or pond-margin plant in frost-free climates, or in between in a humid paludarium. Ruffled, olive-green to bronze lance-shaped leaves emerge from a creeping rhizome that should sit at or just above the substrate surface rather than buried deep, since burying the crown encourages rot. Plants moved between submersed and emersed conditions, or disturbed by a change in water chemistry, commonly shed their leaves in a die-back known as 'crypt melt' before pushing fresh growth from the rhizome within a few weeks, so do not discard a melted plant prematurely. Divide the spreading rhizome mats every year or two to control size and share offsets; in any zone below the tropics, treat it as a container aquatic and bring it indoors before the first frost.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Center for Aquatic and Invasive Plants — Plant Directory

planting.note: Plant in fine, nutrient-rich substrate at a shaded pond edge or bog-filter cell with the crown near the waterline in zone 10-12 gardens; in cooler climates keep as an aquarium or paludarium plant and bring indoors before frost.

directions: 'Green Gecko' is a Sri Lankan-origin selection of Cryptocoryne wendtii prized for its bright, fresh green, deeply crinkled leaves with faint pinkish veining near the leaf base, giving a more luminous, textured look than the straight species. Like other Cryptocoryne, it can be grown fully submersed in an aquarium, emersed at the shaded margin of a warm-climate pond or bog filter, or in a humid paludarium, and it tends to color up brighter under stronger, indirect light without needing supplemental CO2. It is a slow, steady grower that resents being uprooted and moved, often responding to relocation with a temporary leaf die-back before resuming growth from the rhizome, so choose a permanent spot and disturb it as little as possible. Propagate by separating rooted plantlets that form along the spreading rhizome, and protect plants from any temperature below the mid-60s Fahrenheit, since this is a strictly tropical plant with no frost tolerance.

planting.note: Site as a compact shaded foreground marginal at a warm-climate pond edge or bog-filter cell with the crown near the waterline; in cooler climates grow it submersed in an aquarium or emersed in a paludarium and bring it indoors before frost.

directions: Named for the Danish aquatic-plant nursery that popularized it, 'Tropica' is the most compact commonly available Cryptocoryne wendtii cultivar, forming a dense low mound of broad, heavily hammered leaves that shift from deep green to bronze and orange tones depending on light intensity. Its small size makes it well suited to the shaded foreground of a bog-filter cell or the shallow margin of a warm-climate ornamental pond, as well as to aquarium and paludarium use, and it tolerates both fully submersed and fully emersed conditions once established. As with other Cryptocoryne, avoid disturbing established clumps, since transplant shock can trigger a temporary leaf melt that the plant regrows from its rhizome over several weeks. Divide the slowly spreading rhizome to propagate new plants, and protect it year-round from temperatures below the mid-60s Fahrenheit, as it has no cold tolerance outside the tropics.

planting.note: Tie or glue the rhizome to a rock or piece of driftwood at the shaded margin of a warm-climate pond or bog filter with the crown held above the substrate near or just under the waterline; in cooler zones keep it as an aquarium or paludarium plant and overwinter indoors.

directions: This West African forest-stream variety of Anubias barteri is grown for its thick, leathery new leaves that emerge coffee-brown and slowly deepen to dark olive-green as they age, giving established clumps a striking two-tone effect. Like the more common var. nana, it is naturally amphibious, growing along shaded stream banks where it is alternately flooded and exposed, so it thrives either fully submersed in an aquarium, fully emersed at the shady margin of a frost-free outdoor pond or bog filter, or in a humid paludarium spanning both zones. The rhizome must never be buried in substrate or mud, since this causes rot; instead anchor it to hardscape with thread or aquarium-safe glue until roots grip on their own, typically within a month. It is slow-growing and tolerates low light well, making it forgiving in shaded pond corners, but it has no frost tolerance and must be moved to an aquarium or heated greenhouse before temperatures drop in fall outside zone 10-11.

planting.note: Attach the rhizome to a small rock or piece of wood at the shaded, shallow margin of a warm-climate pond or bog-filter cell, or just under the waterline in a container water garden; in cooler zones grow it as an aquarium foreground or paludarium plant year-round.

directions: A Singapore-origin dwarf selection of Anubias barteri var. nana, 'Petite' is the smallest widely available Anubias, forming a dense low mat of tiny, dark green leaves under half an inch across on a slow-creeping rhizome. Its miniature scale suits it to the shaded foreground of a small container water garden or the low margin of a bog-filter cell in frost-free climates, where it can be attached to a small stone or piece of wood right at the waterline; it is equally at home fully submersed in an aquarium or emersed in a shaded paludarium. As with all Anubias, the rhizome must be left exposed on top of the substrate or hardscape rather than buried, since covering it invites rot, and growth is very slow even in ideal warmth and light. It has no cold tolerance and must be kept as an aquarium plant or moved to a heated greenhouse outside its zone 10-11 outdoor range.
